jobs.description: Diese Rolle richtet sich an eine zertifizierte Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit, die Freude daran hat, internationale Arbeitswelten sicherer zu machen und als zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen US‑amerikanischen Exchange‑Strukturen und deutschen/europäischen Arbeitsschutzvorgaben zu agieren.Ihre Aufgaben- Beratung im Arbeitsschutz — Sie unterstützen das Exchange Europe Occupational Health and Safety Program bei der Einhaltung deutscher und europäischer Sicherheitsgesetze und setzen die internen Arbeitsschutzrichtlinien um.- Interpretation und Anwendung von Standards — Sie übertragen nationale Vorschriften sowie OSHA‑Standards in die Exchange‑Strukturen und begleiten deren Umsetzung.- Fachliche Betreuung von Sicherheitsprogrammen — Sie überwachen Programme der industriellen Sicherheit und Präventivmedizin und stellen sicher, dass lokale Sicherheitsstandards in Prozesse und Anweisungen integriert werden.- Zusammenarbeit mit Behörden — Sie pflegen enge Kontakte zu Sicherheitsbehörden, Feuerwehren und Präventionsstellen und fördern die Kooperation in allen sicherheitsrelevanten Bereichen.- Durchführung von Inspektionen — Sie prüfen Einrichtungen, Arbeitsplätze, ergonomische Bedingungen, Arbeitsprozesse und technische Anlagen.- Unfallanalyse — Sie untersuchen Vorfälle, erstellen Berichte und leiten Maßnahmen ab.- Schulungen & Führung — Sie führen Trainings durch und übernehmen die fachliche Leitung von Mitarbeitenden.Ihr Profil- Zertifizierung als Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit nach deutschem Recht- Mindestens 2 Jahre einschlägige Berufserfahrung- Fundierte Kenntnisse im deutschen/europäischen Arbeits- und Gesundheitsschutzrecht- Führerschein Klasse B und Bereitschaft zu Reisetätigkeit- Ausgezeichnete Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und SchriftHinweis: Die Stelle kann auf der Ebene C‑7a besetzt werden, wenn die Qualifikationen noch nicht vollständig erfüllt sind.Schwerbehinderte Bewerberinnen und Bewerber oder Bewerberinnen und Bewerber mit gleichgestelltem Status werden bei gleicher Qualifikation bevorzugt berücksichtigt.++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++The Exchange is part of the U.S. Armed Forces. As a retail organization, the Exchange provides soldiers, civilians, and their family members with all the shopping opportunities they are familiar with from home. In addition to stores offering clothing and everyday necessities, AAFES also operates branded restaurants, movie theaters, and more. The organization also includes a large vehicle fleet, a distribution center, and a bakery.Serves as an Occupational Health & Safety Advisor for the Exchange in Germany.Position incumbent works under general supervision of the Regional Loss Prevention Manager and assists in providing support to the Exchange Europe Occupational Health and Safety Program in complying with host nation safety laws. Complies with Exchange Occupational Health and Safety policies, directives, and regulations.Performs as advisor, technical consultant and coordinator in the application of host nation safety laws and their integration into the Exchange Europe Occupational Health and Safety Program. Interprets safety policies and standards, to include OSHA, for application. Assists with implementation and enforcement of standards. Provides professional guidance on safety requirements.Provides oversight of the Industrial Safety & Preventive Medicine Programs. Assists in ensuring host country safety practices and standards are incorporated into operating procedures, directives, and instructions.Establishes and maintains close liaison with various safety agencies to ensure cooperation with fleet safety, fire protection and prevention, accident prevention, and other matters of concern. Performs plan reviews, conducts compliance inspections to include facilities, equipment, ergonomics and work processes. Advises on the layout of workplaces, processes, and work environment. Recommends corrective actions.Analyzes accidents, conducts investigations, prepares reports and recommendations.May be required to conduct training. Supervises subordinate personnel.MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:Must be certified to act as an Occupational Safety and Health Specialist (Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit) under German law plus a minimum of 2 years’ related work experience. Knowledge of worker-safety provisions of the German/European Labor Safety and Occupational Health laws and rules.Preferred related work experience in the retail field.Position involves travel; driver’s license Class B is required.LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT:Position requires an excellent command of both written and oral English and German language.* Note: Position may be filled at C-7a level if qualifications are not fully met yet.Severely handicapped applicants, or applicants of the same status with the same qualifications, will be given preferential consideration.Ergänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Lärmschutz, Fachtheoretische Unterweisung, GefahrenanalyseExpertenkenntnisse: ErgonomieZwingend erforderlich: Arbeitsmedizin, Arbeitsschutz, Unfallverhütung, Arbeitsplatzanalyse, Arbeitsplatzgestaltung

Company DescriptionAbout us:Passion for food. Hunger for tech. We make METRO digital.Today technology is driving the world. And at METRO.digital we are driving the technology for one of the leading international wholesalers specializing in food - METRO. From e-commerce to checkout, to delivery software, we work on a wide range of products to make each day a success for our customers and colleagues. With passion and ownership, we build the future of wholesale.You are driving to create smart solutions for customers around the globe? You want to grow in a flexible environment? Let the right career opportunity find you and join us!How you will make an impact?The main objective of the LUCA program is to successfully upgrade METRO’s Finance to SAP S/4HANA to ensure business continuity and avoid security and compliance risks. The LUCA program is, in addition, a critical enabler of METRO’s strategy to achieve standardization, harmonization, and centralization.As a Technical Architect within the LUCA program, you will design and implement SAP finance solutions to optimize financial processes, review business requirements to deliver effective and standardized solutions. You will have a focus on Subledgers, namely on Account Receivable processes. Thus, the role requires deep expertise in SAP’s subledgers modules such as AR, AP, SD and Serrala’s Autobank solution, combined with hands-on experience in implementation and application support.Job DescriptionYour Responsibilities:- Collaborate with finance, process, and IT teams to convert requirements into practical technical designs;- Lead project rollouts solutioning of business requirements, from solution design to implementation, while analyzing complex changes and troubleshooting issues;- Ensure solutions align with Metro’s global template, enterprise architecture, SAP best practices, and compliance standards;- Simplify and convey technical concepts to diverse audiences, including executives, business users, and technical teams;- Oversee SI partner delivery by reviewing and approving requirements refinement, high level and detailed design documents, transports, customizing documentation.QualificationsRequired key competencies and qualifications:- Bachelor’s/Master’s in Business Informatics, Computer Science, or related field, with strong knowledge of Financial Accounting and Indirect Procurement;- 10+ years in SAP AP, AR, SD, with familiarity in SAP Fiori and SAP Business Technology Platform and Serrala’s Autobank as a plus;- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills;- Finance-related SAP certifications are advantageous;- Retail industry experience preferred for tailored SAP solutions;- Excellent English proficiency (written and spoken);- Willingness and ability to travel as required.Additional InformationWhat we offer at METRO.digital?- Hybrid and agile work: thrive in a flexible, multicultural environment.At METRO.digital, we promote work-life balance through a hybrid working model. You’ll be part of self-organizing, multicultural teams that collaborate in an agile setup.- People development: when you grow so do we!We want you to become the best version of yourself with individual and company-wide programs and trainings for people development. Focused among other on development, leadership, appreciation ... it´s time to upskill your career.- Support with individual solutions: we are people-caring!We offer support whenever you need it - at every stage of your professional journey.Want to know more about all our benefits? Discover more here (https://metro.digital/about/life-at-metro) .Let´s connect soon. Apply for the role now!Position grade within our career framework: Technical Architect Grade 1 (Md8).

The Leibniz-Institut für Analytische Wissenschaften - ISAS - e. V. develops efficient analytical methods for health research. Thus, it contributes to the improvement of the prevention, early diagnosis, and therapy of diseases like cardiovascular diseases or cancer. Overall, the institute strives to advance precision medicine by combining knowledge from different fields such as biology, chemistry, computer science, medicine, pharmacology, and physics. ISAS is a member of the Leibniz Association and is publicly funded by the Federal Republic of Germany and its federal states.We invite applications for the Research Group Biofluorescence: PhD candidate (f/m/d)This project, funded by the DFG as part of CRC 1752, "DYNAMO: Immediate Tumor Dynamics in Melanoma Therapy“ (https://www.uni-due.de/crc1752/) seeks to combine high-resolution multi-omics profiling, advanced computational modeling, and clinically aligned biomarker stratification, in order to generate actionable, patient-specific predictions and resistance-targeting interventions in melanoma therapy. You will be responsible for finding out the role of neutrophils for the early development of therapy resistance in human melanoma. The project is being carried out in collaboration with University Hospital Essen and the University of Duisburg-Essen.You will be responsible for- Experimental setup and execution of neutrophil functional profiling in the context of melanoma immune regulation and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response- Functional assays of neutrophils including migration, phagocytosis, and ROS production- Optimization and standardization of neutrophil functional assays for primary human samples- Few-cell proteomics for deep molecular characterization of neutrophil subsets- Multicolor flow cytometry of PBMCs and immune cell populations- Live-cell imaging and advanced microscopy for dynamic immune cell behavior analysis- Planning and execution of stimulation and inhibition experiments to dissect signaling pathways regulating neutrophil function in the melanoma context- Data processing, analysis, interpretation, and visualization of experimental results in collaboration with computational partnersYour profile- Completed diploma or master’s degree in molecular biology, cancer biology, immunology, cell biology, bioinformatics, translational medicine or related disciplines- Experience in molecular and cellular biology techniques, ideally with hands-on experience with functional immune cell assays (preferably with neutrophils or myeloid cells) is an advantage- Strong interest in melanoma biology, tumor immunology, immune checkpoint therapy, translational cancer research, and tumor–immune interactions- Experience with cell culture, flow cytometry, microscopy, proteomics workflows or high-dimensional immune profiling approaches is desirable- Experience with bioinformatics or biostatistics is beneficial but not required- Ability to work independently and in interdisciplinary teams, with strong organizational skills and analytical thinking- High level of self-motivation, scientific curiosity, reliability, creativity, and team-oriented personality with enthusiasm to work in a collaborative research environment- Fluent in spoken and written EnglishWe offer- A clear research topic as well as multifold training and support for PhD students in framework of ISAS and the Leibniz association- Opportunities for scientific training and development in an international environment and an excellent working atmosphere in a very dynamic and professional team- Access to state-of-the-art technologies including few-cell proteomics, high-dimensional flow cytometry, and advanced microscopy platforms- Integration into an interdisciplinary, internationally visible, translation-oriented cancer immunology research network- The opportunity to present your data on international conferences and participate in workshops- A wide range of opportunities for further training and qualifications- Flexible working times, mobile working and attractive social benefits- Family-friendly infrastructure and support from a family serviceNon-residents who apply for this job will receive help from the institute to find accommodation and to handle authorities. Applications from disabled applicants are welcome. ISAS supports the principle of equal opportunity for all employees and therefore particularly encourages women to apply.The part-time position (65%) starts on October 1, 2026, and is offered until June 30, 2030. The salary will be according to the German TV-L and falls within the pay group 13. The time limitation of the contract is based on the Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz (WissZeitVG).ISAS collects and processes the personal data of its applicants in accordance with European and German legal regulations. Further information on data protection and the processing of personal data can be found at: https://www.isas.de/en/datenschutz.The closing date for applications is** August 14, 2026**. Please apply via our applicant portal (https://bewerbermanagement.net/en/jobposting/4e342c0b4ebdda805ec07aefc033c1e6bce0d9010/apply?ref=Agentur+f%C3%BCr+Arbeit+Dortmund) . If you have any questions (reference number 411_2026), feel free to contact the Human Resources team (bewerbungen@isas.de). Further information about the institute can be found at: https://www.isas.de/en.

The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.The following full-/part-time position (38.5/19.5 hours per week)  is to be filled as soon as possible in the Institute for Hygiene and Public Health, Section Global Child Health of the University Hospital Bonn:Scientific coordinator (m/f/d)The Section of Global Child Health was established in November 2025 with the appointment of the Endowed Professorship in Global Child Health. The Section’s remit includes research and teaching in Germany and internationally, as well as clinical practice and the applied, practice-oriented engagement with global health challenges affecting children and adolescents. The professorship is structured as a tandem appointment with a corresponding position at the University of Malawi, based in Lilongwe.You will work in close collaboration with the section head in establishing sound research and communication networks with partners in Malawi and GermanyThe professorship focuses on research in the area of neonatal, child, and adolescent health in “Low and Middle Income Countries” (LMICs), identifies barriers to and solutions for improving global child health, and facilitates the transfer of epidemiological and clinical evidence into health care services with the goal of improving the health status of all children globally.It facilitates institutional, national and international networking and collaboration with universities, academic institutions and key development partners.In addition, it provides academic and health policy advice to national and international governmental as well as non-governmental organizations with regard to global child health.The position is initially limited to three years and remunerated according to TV-L EG 13 (German tax ID is a prerequisite). If you currently live abroad, you should be willing to relocate to Germany temporarily. Subject to interest and feasibility, a temporary increase in the scope of employment through third-party funded resources is envisaged.Tasks:This position offers the opportunity to actively contribute to the development of global strategies for improving children's health and to build and design a completely new international research and education structure.- Strategic coordination and management of international research, education and clinical programmes across the two professorships and the EKFS network- Planning, coordination, and monitoring of cross-institutional activities with academic and non-academic partners- Management of communication channels between institutions, disciplines, and countries, ensuring efficient information flow and alignment of activities- Coordination, and implementation of training materials and structured capacity-building programmes in collaboration with international experts- Planning, organisation, and delivery of international workshops and seminars in online and on-site formats- Preparation of annual progress and impact reports, dissemination of results through conferences and other scientific communication formats- Contribution to the strategic development, coordination, and drafting of third-party funding proposals to expand and sustain programme activitiesRequirements:- A full academic degree at Master’s level or higher in a health-related discipline- A strong interest in global child health and international health systems cooperation- Demonstrated experience in project coordination and research management- Excellent organisational skills and a structured, meticulous approach to work- Proven ability to navigate academic hierarchies and university administrative processes, combined with sensitivity to intercultural contexts- Strong teamwork skills, resilience, and the ability to assert and represent set positions- Full professional proficiency in both German and English, written and spoken Willingness to jobs.occupation: PhD Position : Clinical and Multi-Omics Biomarker Discovery and Risk Prediction in Diabetes Compli-cations
jobs.description:
We invite applications for an exciting PhD position within the Bioinformatics and Data Science Team, Complications Research Group, Clinical and Translational Research Department at Steno Diabetes Center Copenhagen (SDCC).

This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of clinical research, multi-omics, computational biology and precision medicine, contributing to the discovery of novel biomarkers and improved risk prediction of diabetes-related complications.

About the Complications Research Group

The Complications Research Group is led by a research manager and currently comprises five senior scientists, together with several PhD students and postdoctoral researchers. Our overall aim is to identify novel biomarkers, mechanisms and risk-stratification approaches to improve the prevention and treatment of microvascular and macrovascular complications of diabetes.

The group includes two clinical research teams and a Bioinformatics and Data Science Team. The latter leads and collaborates on national and international research projects focusing on risk stratification and precision medicine in individuals with type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Our research spans several diabetes complications, including neuropathy, brain and cognitive dysfunction, cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, diabetic foot disease and retinopathy.

Our research integrates clinical cohort data with multi-omics technologies and advanced bioinformatics, statistical and artificial intelligence approaches. We specialize in human genomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics to identify novel disease mechanisms, biomarkers and therapeutic targets, ultimately supporting improved clinical decision-making and personalized medicine.

About the Project

This PhD project will focus on translational biomarker discovery and risk prediction of neurological complications and neurodegeneration in individuals with type 2 diabetes.

The project will involve the acquisition and analysis of metabolomics and lipidomics data from well-characterised clinical cohorts, alongside integration with other molecular and clinical data. You will receive training in omics data processing, multi-modal data integration, computational biology and advanced data science approaches, including machine learning.

Joining our team, you will become an integral part of a multi-omics research initiative within the Complications Research Group, working closely with clinicians and researchers across SDCC. The project will be conducted within the Bioinformatics and Data Science Team, in collaboration with the Type 2 Diabetes and Neuro Unit at SDCC and other research partners.

The Position and Your Responsibilities: As a PhD student, you will take an active role in the planning, execution and dissemination of research findings. Your responsibilities will include:

• Contributing to the acquisition, processing and quality control of metabolomics and lipidomics data.

• Managing and analysing complex clinical and multi-omics datasets.

• Developing and applying computational pipelines for multi-modal data integration, including clinical, imaging and omics data.

• Conducting biomarker discovery, mechanistic investigations and risk-prediction analyses.

• Applying statistical modelling, machine learning and other advanced data science approaches.

• Preparing scientific manuscripts, presenting research findings and contributing to collaborative research activities.

We are looking for a motivated candidate with the following qualifications:

• A Master's degree in Bioinformatics, Biomedical Engineering, Computational Biology, Data Science or a related discipline.

• A strong interest in biomedical research, omics technologies and precision medicine.

• Knowledge of metabolomics and/or lipidomics/proteomics, preferably with experience in omics data analysis and AI/ML implementation within a clinical setting.

• Good programming and analytical skills, preferably in R and/or Python.

• An interest in multi-omics data integration, statistical modelling and machine learning/AI approaches.

Previous research experience, scientific publications and experience with clinical or omics datasets will be considered an advantage.

We particularly welcome candidates who are enthusiastic about combining computational and analytical approaches with clinically relevant research.

What We Offer

We offer an exciting opportunity to develop a research career at the interface of bioinformatics, multi-omics and clinical translational research.

You will benefit from:

• Working in an interdisciplinary research environment with close interaction between bioinformaticians, clinicians and experimental researchers.

• Access to well-characterised clinical cohorts and advanced omics technologies.

• Training in multi-omics data integration, computational biology, machine learning and precision medicine.

• Opportunities to participate in national and international research collaborations involving academia and industry.

• Opportunities to develop independent research ideas, contribute to grant applications and establish your own research profile.

• Formal training and opportunities to develop scientific, project-management and leadership skills.

Recruitment and Employment

Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement for Academics employed by the Danish Regions (Danske Regioner) and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (Akademikerne).

Contact and Application: Applications must be submitted online by 15 December 2026.

Interviews are expected to take place during the following week, with an anticipated starting date of 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

For further information about the position, kindly contact: Associate Professor Tarunveer Singh Ahluwalia, the Bioinformatics and Data Science group lead or Professor Tine W. Hansen, Head of Department, Complications Research, SDCC.

We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds who possess the relevant academic qualifications and motivation.

About Steno Diabetes Center Copenhagen

Steno Diabetes Center Copenhagen (SDCC) is a leading centre for diabetes care, research, prevention and education of healthcare professionals. SDCC is the largest diabetes clinic in Scandinavia, providing specialised care to more than 11,000 children and adults with diabetes annually. Through close integration of clinical practice and research, SDCC aims to advance diabetes prevention, treatment and personalised medicine.

jobs.occupation: Associate Professorship at the Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research
jobs.description:
The Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, Aarhus University, invites applications for Associate Professorship in social science alcohol and drug research, commencing 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research is an independent, interdisciplinary social science research centre. As an Associate Professor, you are expected to conduct high-quality research that strengthens the Centre’s research environment and contributes to the development of alcohol and drug research in Denmark. You will be expected to help strengthen the Centre’s international, including Nordic, research profile and collaborative activities within the field.

Candidates are expected to attract external research funding, publish in recognised academic journals and book series, teach at undergraduate and graduate levels, supervise PhD students, and have experience in, or shortly after appointment take responsibility for, leading research projects. There is also an expectation that you actively disseminate alcohol and drug research in a Danish context to practitioners, policymakers, and the general public. Furthermore, it is a requirement that you are based at the Centre on a daily basis and contribute actively and enthusiastically to its interdisciplinary research environment. Administrative duties will also be associated with the position.

Qualifications

Applicants with a social science research background in alcohol and drug studies and related areas will be preferred. Appointment as Associate Professor furthermore requires research and teaching qualifications equivalent to those typically achieved through a successful period of employment as an Assistant Professor although equivalent qualifications may also have been acquired through other means. To obtain permanent employment as an Associate Professor at Aarhus BSS, candidates must, prior to appointment, have completed the faculty’s supervision course and the faculty’s course in Online and Blended Learning offered by the Centre for Educational Development at Aarhus University. If these courses have not been completed prior to employment, appointment will be conditional upon their completion within five years.

About Us

At the Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, we conduct social science research within the field of alcohol and drug studies. Our research projects focus on areas including treatment, prevention and harm reduction, policy, law enforcement, and recreational substance use. We study both legal and illegal substances. The Centre is interdisciplinary, and staff members have backgrounds in fields such as anthropology, psychology, sociology, criminology, and public health. Our aim is to establish and conduct research projects, provide teaching, disseminate knowledge about alcohol and drug problems, develop interventions, and collaborate with national stakeholders and international research institutions. For more information about the Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, please visit www.crf.au.dk.

The Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research is part of the Department of Psychology, Aarhus BSS, Aarhus University. The Department of Psychology is one of six departments within Aarhus BSS, one of the University’s five faculties. Aarhus BSS brings together the core business and social science disciplines to reflect the close relationship between society and business. Aarhus University is ranked among the world’s top 100 universities, and Aarhus BSS and the Department of Psychology have obtained the prestigious AACSB and AMBA accreditations.

Further Information

For further information regarding the position, please contact: Bagga Bjerge, Director, Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, Tel.: +45 22 35 19 89. Email: bb.crf@psy.au.dk

If you require assistance with uploading your application or have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact: Charlotte Thomsen, HR-Coordinator. Tel.: +45 87 16 53 62. Email: Charlotte@au.dk.

The place of employment is: Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, Bartholins Allé 9, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark

Application deadline
12 January 2027

International applicant? 
Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information here:
https://internationalstaff.au.dk/relocationservice/

Please find more information about research opportunities at Aarhus University here: http://international.au.dk/research/

Terms of employment
Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as associate professor at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).

The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

Application procedure
When you apply for this position it is mandatory to attach the following:

• Application
• Curriculum Vitae. You are encouraged to declare any periods of leave without research activity, including, for example, maternity leave, since your research activities are assessed in relation to your actual research time
• Education (diploma for master's, PhD and possibly higher doctoral degree)
• List of publications (the enclosed publications must be clearly marked on the list of publications)
• Publications. Up to five publications can be included in the application. In the event of several authors the publications must be accompanied by a co-author statement concerning the applicant's share of the collaborative work with the consent of the co-authors. This template may be used for the purpose
• Teaching portfolio. The specific requirements regarding the documentation can be found here
 Materials which cannot be uploaded together with the application may be submitted in five copies to Aarhus BSS HR & PhD, Aarhus University, Bartholins Allé 16, DK-8000 Aarhus C.

Read more about how to apply for an academic post at Aarhus BSS here

The evaluation process
After the application deadline, an assessment committee is appointed. Please note that the assessment of applicants is based solely on the material received prior to the application deadline. For further information, see Guidelines for Assessment Committee, Aarhus BSS.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk
